title: The Autopsy of the Marlowe Estate
premise: Retired detective Beatrix Halloran receives two letters about the unsolved Marlowe Estate deaths of 1994: one from someone confessing to the murders, and a second promising that 'the tide will give back what it took.' When a body washes up matching the letter's promise exactly, Beatrix is dragged back into the case that ended his career. As he investigates, he realizes the killer is someone who has studied the original file obsessively — perhaps someone inside the old investigation itself. The trail leads to his former partner, Edmund Voss, who falsified evidence to protect the man he loved; Beatrix must choose between exposing him and letting justice die with the truth. In the end, Beatrix traps the killer at the drowned estate during a spring tide, choosing a confession over an arrest, and finally lays his own guilt over the botched original case to rest.
about_author: O. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former coastal coroner's assistant who spent eleven years cataloguing unexplained deaths along the northern seaboard before turning to fiction. They write in a lighthouse-keeper's cottage and claim every novel begins with a real case file they were never allowed to close.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Beatrix Halloran, dusting the shelves of his failing bookshop, opens two letters postmarked the same day: a full confession to the 1994 Marlowe Estate deaths, and a taunting note promising 'more when the tide turns.' Both are written in handwriting Beatrix half-recognizes. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: dread reawakening a life he buried.

chapters.title: The File He Wasn't Supposed to Keep
chapters.summary: Beatrix retrieves his illegal copy of the original Marlowe case file from a floor safe beneath the shop's poetry section. Three deaths: patriarch Alistair Marlowe, his nurse, and a missing boy never found. POV: Beatrix, with flashbacks. Emotional beat: shame — the case broke him and ended his career in disgrace.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought In
chapters.summary: Police call Beatrix to the estuary: a body washed ashore wearing Alistair Marlowe's signet ring, killed with a method only the 1994 file describes. Detective Inspector Sorcha Nwosu, sharp and skeptical, wants to know how the killer knew details sealed for thirty years. POV: alternating Beatrix and Sorcha. Emotional beat: the past made flesh.

chapters.title: The House That Drowns Twice a Day
chapters.summary: Beatrix visits the derelict Marlowe Estate, reachable only at low tide, and finds fresh footprints and a single white carnation on the staircase where the nurse died. Someone still tends the house like a shrine. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: grief dressed as investigation.

chapters.title: Everyone Signed the Same Oath
chapters.summary: Beatrix tracks down surviving members of the original investigative team. Each received a letter too — each confessed something small and private in reply. The killer has been collecting confessions for years. POV: Beatrix interviewing witnesses. Emotional beat: paranoia; no one is clean.

chapters.title: Sorcha's Doubt
chapters.summary: DI Nwosu discovers Beatrix withheld his letters and confronts him, threatening obstruction charges. Forced into uneasy alliance, she reveals the new victim was the retired forensic tech from the original case. POV: Sorcha. Emotional beat: reluctant trust between two people who both distrust institutions.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Was Never Found
chapters.summary: Beatrix reconstructs the ignored thread of the case: ten-year-old Caspian Marlowe, listed as runaway, whose disappearance was quietly closed after forty-eight hours. Beatrix remembers signing off on it. POV: Beatrix, memory-heavy. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Letters from the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: A third letter arrives, addressed not to Beatrix but to 'the boy's true friend,' containing a child's drawing of the estate and a date: the spring equinox tide. The killer is counting down. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: being chosen, and what that costs.

chapters.title: Edmund
chapters.summary: Beatrix visits his estranged former partner Edmund Voss, now dying slowly in a care home by the sea. Their conversation is warm and barbed; Edmund quotes case details he shouldn't remember so precisely. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: old love, old suspicion, indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Nurse's Sister
chapters.summary: The murdered nurse's sister, Maren, runs a seaside boarding house and keeps a box of her sibling's effects — including a diary page torn out, its stub matching paper used in the killer's letters. She lies about when she last saw it. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the first human suspect, and the first human sorrow.

chapters.title: Archive Fire
chapters.summary: The county records office burns overnight; the original Marlowe file is destroyed. Only Beatrix's illegal copy survives — making him either the last witness or the perfect suspect. Sorcha must formally consider him. POV: Sorcha. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under the alliance.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: A storm knocks out power during Sorcha's interview of Beatrix. By candlelight, he finally tells her the whole truth of 1994: evidence he was ordered to ignore, the closed search for Caspian, the career-ending report he never filed. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: confession as relief and weaponization.

chapters.title: What Edmund Protected
chapters.summary: Following the diary page, Beatrix learns the nurse discovered Alistair Marlowe had been abusing Caspian — and that someone powerful buried it. Edmund's falsified evidence wasn't corruption; it was protection, though of whom remains unclear. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: love against duty, the theme made explicit.

chapters.title: Maren's Second Lie
chapters.summary: Sorcha catches Maren in a contradiction: she was at the estate the night the forensic tech died. Under pressure, Maren admits receiving letters for years — confessions she answered because the writer claimed to be Caspian, alive. POV: Sorcha. Emotional beat: hope weaponized against the grieving.

chapters.title: Caspian, Alive or Otherwise
chapters.summary: Beatrix digs into records and finds a boy matching Caspian's description adopted out under a sealed order signed by a judge connected to the Marlowe family. The confession letter's phrasing echoes a child's testimony transcript. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: vertigo — the victim may be the killer.

chapters.title: The Trap That Requires Bait
chapters.summary: Beatrix proposes using himself: he'll publish, via the bookshop window, a fabricated detail claiming the final letter's promised 'last gift' has been found. Only the true keeper of the file's secrets would react. Sorcha agrees, terrified. POV: Sorcha. Emotional beat: crossing the line justice forbids.

chapters.title: Night Visit
chapters.summary: Someone enters the bookshop at night but takes nothing, leaving instead a photograph: young Beatrix and Edmund outside the estate in 1994, with a third figure half-cropped from the frame. On the back: 'You always cropped him out.' POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: hunted in his own sanctuary.

chapters.title: The Third Figure
chapters.summary: Photo analysis and Edmund's failing memory converge: the cropped figure is the judge's son, the man who took Caspian away and later returned as the estate's quiet caretaker. Edmund protected Beatrix from knowing how deep the cover-up ran. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Equinox Eve
chapters.summary: The killer summons Beatrix directly: come alone to the estate at high tide, bring the file, bring the truth. Sorcha plans a covert approach; Beatrix knows the tides will betray them all if timing slips. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: calm before the drowning.

chapters.title: The Autopsy of the Marlowe Estate
chapters.summary: In the flooding house, Beatrix faces the killer — Caspian, grown, who has staged each death as a reconstruction of his own erased suffering. He wants not escape but a full accounting, witnessed. The tide rises; Sorcha is cut off; Edmund arrives unexpectedly in his wheelchair-accessible van. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: climax — judgment demanded outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: As water fills the ground floor, Beatrix offers Caspian what the law never could: he reads aloud, on record, everything the file and the family concealed, naming every adult who failed him. Caspian surrenders the knife; Edmund collapses; Sorcha reaches them as the tide peaks. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: catharsis — truth as the only verdict available.

chapters.title: Low Tide, Open Shop
chapters.summary: Weeks later: Caspian awaits trial, Edmund dies holding Beatrix's hand, and Sorcha closes the case with the confession intact. Beatrix reopens the bookshop with a new shelf — books on memory and tide tables — and mails one last letter of his own: an apology to the boy he failed in 1994. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; justice outside the law, love outlasting duty.
